title: Research program: which signal pairings differ from their null during omission, and which bands lead

goal.text: Establish which pairs of signals -- band power to band power, band power to spiking, within and between channels, areas and animals -- carry a relationship during omission that a shuffle-corrected null does not produce, and which bands lead which in time.
goal.falsifier: Closed when, for each declared pairing, either a null-corrected effect is reported with its lag and its volume-conduction control, or the pairing is reported as null with the power to detect a stated effect size.

notes: SCOPE. Omission paradigm, three macaques sampled without selection on outcome, ten analysis areas (V1, V2, V3a/d, V4, MT, MST, TEO, FST, FEF, PFC), 23 sessions carrying time-frequency products, 9,344 channels with a disjoint area assignment, 9,228 spike-sorted units. Signals available: LFP band power (five bands), spike trains, MUAe. Layer labels exist for 58 per cent of channels and 30.5 per cent of units.

THE GENERAL QUESTION, as Hamm framed it: is there any correlation between two events, or between two signals during one event, that differs from a shuffle or null control? The pairings enumerated are band power to band power, within or between area, within or between animal, within or between channel.

QUESTION 1 -- PAIRWISE BAND-POWER COUPLING. For each band, and each context (pre-trial baseline, stimulus present, omitted slot, post-omission delay, random-control condition), estimate the coupling between band-power time courses for every channel pair, and compare against a trial-shuffled null in which the pairing between trials is broken but each channel's own autocorrelation is preserved. The quantity of interest is the CHANGE in coupling between contexts, not its absolute level, because the absolute level is dominated by anatomy and by shared reference.

QUESTION 2 -- IS THE COUPLING GRAPH NON-TRIVIAL. Volume conduction produces zero-lag, zero-phase coupling between nearby channels and can manufacture an entire apparent network. Any coupling claim on this corpus must be robust to it. Three controls, in increasing order of strength: bipolar derivation by nearest-neighbour laminar differencing before any cross-site comparison, which the Methods already require; discarding the zero-lag component by using the imaginary part of coherency or orthogonalised power envelopes; and demonstrating a non-zero lag, which volume conduction cannot produce because it is instantaneous. A coupling result reported without at least the second of these is not separable from field spread.

QUESTION 3 -- WHICH BANDS LEAD, AND WHEN. Direction requires a lag-resolved measure: the phase-slope index, the lag of the peak cross-correlation between band-power envelopes, or a directed spectral measure. 'When' requires the estimate to be time-resolved across the omission window rather than averaged over it, because the field response is a ramp that continues into the following delay rather than resolving inside the omitted slot.

WHAT THE DESIGN ALREADY CONSTRAINS. Four results established earlier today bound every one of these analyses and must be carried into each: (a) animal is the dominant term for band power, raising explained variance from 0.09 to 0.70 in alpha when added to an area-only model, so any coupling statistic must be estimated within animal before it is pooled; (b) the channel-to-area partition assigns equal shares of each probe and is an assumption, so between-area coupling for channels near a segment boundary inherits that assumption; (c) layer coverage is unbalanced across animals at P = 0.0017 and varies about threefold across areas, so a laminar coupling contrast is interpretable only within an animal and an area; (d) the unit of inference is the session, because channels on one shank are not independent.

MEASURE-ORDER HAZARD. The same averaging-order trap that inverted the band-power result applies to coupling. Correlations and coherences must be combined across trials, channels and sessions in a defined order, and a Fisher z transform applied before averaging correlation coefficients. Averaging raw correlations, like averaging decibels, is biased by the variance of the quantity being averaged.

SPIKE-FIELD PAIRING (figure 6). Two directions are being asked, and they are different questions: does band power at time t predict a unit's firing at t + tau, and does a unit's firing predict band power at t + tau. Both need the same shuffle correction and the same lag resolution, and both need the spike-channel distance controlled, since a unit's own spikes contaminate the LFP recorded on its own and neighbouring channels in the gamma range.

FIGURE MAPPING. Question 1 and 2 are figure 5 as specified: four panels, baseline, stimulus present, omission, and shuffle, each an area-by-layer coupling matrix. Question 3 is the directional extension. Spike-field pairing is figure 6. The unit-level band-power relationship by response class is figure 7 in its revised form.
issues: READINESS UPDATE 2026-08-04. The estimator layer for Question 3 now exists and is validated on synthetic ground truth (jnwb_directed_connectivity_20260804: granger, granger_spectral, phase_slope_index, transfer_entropy, directed_network). This closes 'the lag estimate' half of the 'no code exists yet' issue below. It does NOT close the program. Four gaps remain between the estimators and a result on this corpus, and none is a re-run: (1) no session-level extraction path feeds them -- see the raw-LFP issue below; (2) bipolar / nearest-neighbour laminar differencing, which the Methods require before any cross-site comparison, is still unimplemented, so PSI's volume-conduction robustness is currently the only field-spread control in play and the program calls that the second of three, not the first; (3) directed_network pools whatever array it is handed and has no within-animal or within-session grouping layer, while constraint (a) makes within-animal estimation mandatory before pooling and (d) makes session the unit of inference; (4) the power to detect a coupling change is still unestablished, so a null from these estimators cannot yet be reported as absence.

RAW LFP IS NOT ACCESSIBLE THROUGH THE SESSION API (verified 2026-08-04). jnwb/session.py exposes lfp_channel_areas, tfr_from_preprocessed, lfp_tfr_trace_suite_omission and lfp_tfr_trace_correlation -- all TFR-derived. There is no raw-trace accessor. Consequence for the directed estimators: what can run today is band-power time courses at fs = 100 Hz (tfr_from_preprocessed contract: times = -1000 + arange(500)*10 ms, i.e. 10 ms steps, Nyquist 50 Hz), plus spike trains via bin_spikes. That suits Questions 1 and 3, which are about band power, but it means anyone reaching for a raw-LFP directed analysis must first write the NWB extraction.

ENVELOPE-BAND TRAP (2026-08-04). A band-power time course is an ENVELOPE, not the carrier. Passing bands='canonical' or any Hz-valued carrier band to phase_slope_index/granger_spectral on envelope data is a category error twice over: the carrier bands are already integrated out, and at fs = 100 Hz everything above 50 Hz is beyond Nyquist so low_gamma and high_gamma cannot be represented at all. Envelope analyses must state their band argument in envelope-frequency terms (roughly 0-10 Hz) and say so in the caption. The risk is now higher, not lower, because CANONICAL_BANDS was just made the default in jnwb.spectral.cross_area_coherence and jnwb.factories.

Figure 5 as specified is a 20 x 20 matrix over ten areas by two layers. Layer coverage will not support every cell equally: V1 has three deep units and 32 per cent channel coverage against MST at 91 per cent, so cell-to-cell differences would partly encode which cells converged. A 10 x 10 area-only matrix with the laminar split in a supplement, or a stated coverage floor per cell, is the honest form.
No code exists yet for pairwise coupling, for the imaginary-coherency or orthogonalisation controls, or for the lag estimate. This is new implementation, not a re-run.
The corpus contains repeated recordings from the same animals across days. A coupling estimate pooled over sessions treats them as independent; session must remain the unit of inference.

Trial counts per omission condition are low by design, and coupling estimators are more data-hungry than power estimators. The power to detect a coupling change has not been established and should be stated before a null result is reported as absence.

Volume conduction is not the only trivial explanation. A shared reference, a common noise source, and a shared arousal fluctuation each produce broad, non-specific coupling; the context contrast controls the last of these only if the contexts are matched for arousal.
plan: Implement pairwise band-power coupling with a trial-shuffled null, computed within session and within animal, on bipolar-derived signals.
Add the imaginary-coherency or orthogonalised-envelope control and report the zero-lag and non-zero-lag components separately.
Estimate lag by phase-slope index or cross-correlation peak, time-resolved across the omission window and the following delay.
Decide the figure-5 granularity with Hamm: 10 x 10 areas, or 20 x 20 with a per-cell coverage floor.
Extend to spike-field pairing with the spike-channel distance controlled.

verification.receipt: No analysis has been run for this program. This node records the questions and the constraints they inherit from results established on 2026-07-28; it carries no findings and its status is open. The constraints cited are receipted in the nodes listed under links.

links.reasoning: Supplies the validated estimator layer for Question 3 (which bands lead). Partially closes this program's 'no code exists yet' issue -- the lag/direction estimators exist; the extraction, bipolar-derivation, grouping and power layers do not.
Animal dominance means every coupling statistic must be estimated within animal before pooling.
Sets what a laminar coupling matrix can and cannot claim, and why the 20 x 20 form is problematic.
Between-area coupling inherits the equal-share partition assumption for channels near boundaries.
The same averaging-order hazard applies to correlations and coherences; Fisher z before averaging is the analogue of taking the logarithm last.
Supplies figures 5, 6 and the revised 7 for the manuscript.
